09:00.headline: Catchers: is pop time everything?
09:00.topic: Recruiting Reality Check: catcher evaluation beyond pop time (receiving, blocking, accuracy, leadership)

graphic.headline: Catchers: is pop time *everything?*
graphic.sub: It gets the attention. Coaches also watch receiving, blocking, accuracy and how he runs a game.

captions.instagram:
Recruiting Reality Check: if your son catches, is pop time the only number that matters?

Pop time gets the headlines. It's one of the first things a coach notices. But it's only part of how catchers get evaluated.

What coaches also watch:
⚾ Receiving: does he hold strikes quietly?
⚾ Blocking: does he keep balls in the dirt in front of him?
⚾ Accuracy: does the throw arrive on the bag, not just fast?
⚾ Leadership: does he run the game and handle his pitchers?

A quick pop with a wild throw doesn't help much. Make sure his video shows the whole job, not just one throw.

captions.facebook:
Recruiting Reality Check for catcher parents: is pop time everything?

It's the number everyone asks about, and it matters. A strong, quick arm gets a coach's attention.

But when coaches evaluate a catcher, they're looking at the whole job:

⚾ Receiving. Does he catch the ball quietly and give his pitcher a chance at the borderline strike?
⚾ Blocking. Do balls in the dirt stay in front of him?
⚾ Accuracy. A fast throw that pulls the shortstop off the bag isn't an out.
⚾ Leadership. Does he communicate, manage his pitchers and take charge behind the plate?

A practical step this winter: when you put together his video, include receiving and blocking reps along with throws to second. That gives a coach the full picture.

Catcher parents, what has your son's coach told him to work on most? And if you have a recruiting question you'd like us to tackle in a future Reality Check, leave it in the comments.

13:00.headline: Outfielders: beyond the catch
13:00.topic: What coaches evaluate in outfielders: first step/range, routes, arm, bat

captions.instagram:
Outfielders: a highlight catch is great. Coaches are watching what happens before it.

What coaches look at in an outfielder:
1️⃣ First step and range: how quickly he reads the ball off the bat
2️⃣ Routes: does he take a clean line, or drift and recover?
3️⃣ Arm: strength and accuracy hitting the cutoff or the bag
4️⃣ The bat: outfielders are usually expected to hit

The diving catch makes the reel. The clean route that made it easy is what coaches notice.

Save this for his next video session, and share it with an outfielder's parent.

captions.facebook:
What do college coaches actually evaluate in an outfielder?

Parents often focus on the highlight catch. Coaches are usually watching the plays that look routine.

⚾ First step and range. How fast does he read the ball off the bat and get moving?
⚾ Routes. Does he take an efficient line to the ball, or drift and have to recover?
⚾ Arm strength and accuracy. Can he hit the cutoff man or the bag on a line?
⚾ A bat that plays. Outfield is an offensive position at most programs, so his hitting numbers matter too.

Speed helps everywhere out there, but a fast player with poor reads can look slow, and a good reader can look faster than his 60 time.

If he's building a skills video, include a few balls off the bat (not just fungo catches), throws to bases and some at-bats. That's closer to what a coach wants to see.

Outfield parents: what part of his game has improved the most this year?
